findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public network address. Although the shown security group limits MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, public exposure unnecessarily expands the database attack surface and can become externally reachable if security-group rules change.
The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and its snapshots unencrypted at rest. Unauthorized access to underlying storage or backups could expose database contents.

The EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its instance-profile credentials would allow broad control and data access across these AWS services.

The database password is interpolated into EC2 user_data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. This exposes a long-lived database credential through Terraform state and to processes or users able to retrieve instance user data or read the deployed file.

The database security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This creates unnecessary outbound attack surface and enables unrestricted exfiltration or command-and-control traffic if the database host is compromised.
